$\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}={y}^{2}-2y-15$
are

${y}_{1}(t)=$

feedback.worked_solution:
Given an autonomous differential equation ${y}^{′}(t)=f(y),$ if there exists a constant $c$ such that $f(c)=0,$ then $y=c$ is an equilibrium solution of the equation.

So, to find the equilibrium solutions of a differential equation, we must find all values of $c$ such that $f(c)=0.$

In our case, we have that $f(y)={y}^{2}-2y-15,$ so we solve the equation $f(c)=0,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(c) & =0 \\ {c}^{2}-2c-15 & =0 \\ (c-5)(c+3) & =0 \\ c & =-3,5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, in ascending order, ${y}_{1}(t)=-3$ and ${y}_{2}(t)=5$ are the equilibrium solutions of the given differential equation.
